important_note: Dong Kingman died in 2000, so his life+70 copyright term runs until 2070 - the OVERWHELMING MAJORITY of his catalog is still under copyright and was deliberately NOT downloaded. The Met, SFMOMA, and other institutions explicitly mark most Kingman works '© Dong Kingman' or 'rights reserved'. Only two narrow categories of exception were found and are documented per-image below. If a Kingman image is wanted beyond what's here, it almost certainly requires a licensing request to the rightsholder (his estate) or the holding museum.

license_categories.1_public_domain: Watercolors Kingman painted 1935-1942 while employed by the WPA Federal Art Project in California. Under 17 U.S.C. §§ 101 and 105, works made by federal employees/programs as part of official duties are US Government works and are NOT eligible for copyright at all - this is a distinct legal basis from Kingman's personal death date and is explicitly documented via the {{PD-USGov-WPA}} rationale on Wikimedia Commons (verified by reading the template's own legal explanation, not just the category name).
license_categories.2_institution_noncommercial_license: Digitized images from the Smithsonian American Art Museum (SAAM) website, used under SAAM's own stated site-wide terms: "Personal, educational and non-commercial use of digital images from our website is permitted, with attribution to the Smithsonian American Art Museum, for all images unless otherwise noted." (https://americanart.si.edu/art/reproductions). This does NOT mean the underlying artwork is public domain - Kingman's copyright likely still applies - it means SAAM, as the institution holding and having photographed the physical object, permits personal/non-commercial reproduction of ITS digital image. This project (a personal, non-commercial e-ink picture frame) qualifies. These images may NOT be used commercially or redistributed beyond personal use.

excluded_example: File:Dong Kingman - Kearney Street (San Francisco) - 43.104 - Detroit Institute of Arts.jpg was found on Wikimedia Commons tagged {{PD-old-100-1923}}, but this tag was judged to be a MISAPPLIED template (it assumes an artist/work old enough to be pre-1923, which does not fit a work painted in 1940 by an artist who died in 2000) and was deliberately excluded rather than trusted at face value - exactly the kind of name-based/tag-based assumption this research was told to avoid.
